title: Joshua Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 7.

questions.question: Who committed a trespass in the accursed thing according to Joshua 7?
questions.correctAnswer: Achan
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:1 states that Achan, son of Carmi, took of the accursed thing, causing the LORD's anger to be kindled.

questions.question: From which city did Joshua send men to spy out Ai?
questions.correctAnswer: Jericho
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:2 says Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai to view the country.

questions.question: How many men did Joshua send to smite Ai based on the spies' report?
questions.correctAnswer: Two or three thousand
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:3 records the spies advising to send about two or three thousand men to smite Ai.

questions.question: What happened to the men of Israel who went up to Ai?
options: They fled before the men of Ai
questions.correctAnswer: They fled before the men of Ai
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:4 states the about three thousand men fled before the men of Ai.

questions.question: How many Israelites were killed by the men of Ai?
questions.correctAnswer: Thirty and six
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:5 records that thirty and six men of Israel were smitten by Ai.

questions.question: What was the emotional state of the people after the defeat at Ai?
options: Their hearts melted and became as water
questions.correctAnswer: Their hearts melted and became as water
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:5 describes the hearts of the people melting and becoming as water after the defeat.

questions.question: What did Joshua do when he heard of the defeat at Ai?
options: Rent his clothes and fell to the earth before the ark
questions.correctAnswer: Rent his clothes and fell to the earth before the ark
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:6 states Joshua rent his clothes and fell on his face before the ark of the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua prayed to God asking why He brought Israel over Jordan to be defeated by the Amorites.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:7 shows Joshua lamenting why the LORD brought the people over Jordan only to be delivered into the hands of the Amorites.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 7, the men of Israel were victorious against Ai.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:4-5 makes clear that the Israelites fled and were defeated by Ai.

questions.question: What concern did Joshua express about Israel turning their backs before their enemies?
options: That the Canaanites would hear and surround them
That they would win the battle
questions.correctAnswer: That the Canaanites would hear and surround them
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:9 states Joshua was concerned the Canaanites would hear of their defeat and surround them, cutting off their name from the earth.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua put dust upon his head as a sign of mourning.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:6 says Joshua and the elders put dust upon their heads as a sign of mourning.

questions.question: Which place is Ai located near, according to Joshua 7?
options: Beside Bethaven, on the east side of Bethel
questions.correctAnswer: Beside Bethaven, on the east side of Bethel
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:2 describes Ai as beside Bethaven on the east side of Bethel.

questions.question: What was the LORD's reaction to Israel's trespass in the accursed thing?
options: His anger was kindled against the children of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: His anger was kindled against the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:1 states the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel because of Achan's sin.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua commanded all the people to go up and fight Ai without exception.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:3 records that the spies advised not to send all the people, but only two or three thousand men.

questions.question: What did Joshua and the elders do until eventide after hearing the news of defeat?
options: Fell to the earth upon their faces before the ark
questions.correctAnswer: Fell to the earth upon their faces before the ark
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:6 states that Joshua and the elders fell upon their faces before the ark until eventide.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What reason did the LORD give Joshua for Israel's defeat and inability to stand before their enemies?
options: They had taken of the accursed thing and transgressed the covenant
They were outnumbered by their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They had taken of the accursed thing and transgressed the covenant
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:11 explains that Israel sinned by taking the accursed thing, transgressing the covenant, which caused their defeat as stated in Joshua 7:12.

questions.question: According to Joshua 7:12, what condition did God set for His continued presence with Israel?
options: They must destroy the accursed from among them
They must build a new altar
They must fast and pray for seven days
questions.correctAnswer: They must destroy the accursed from among them
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states God will not be with Israel unless they remove the accursed thing from among them, linking the people's sin with His presence.

questions.question: What did God instruct Joshua to do to the people before the next day?
options: Prepare for battle and arm themselves
Sanctify themselves and be ready for the removal of the accursed
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctify themselves and be ready for the removal of the accursed
questions.explanation: In Joshua 7:13, God commands Joshua to sanctify the people for the next day to remove the accursed thing, emphasizing purification before judgment.

questions.question: How was the process of identifying the guilty person to be carried out according to Joshua 7:14?
options: By casting lots among the elders
By bringing people tribe by tribe, family by family, household by household, and man by man
By a public vote of the people
questions.correctAnswer: By bringing people tribe by tribe, family by family, household by household, and man by man
questions.explanation: Verse 14 details a systematic approach to find the guilty person, showing God's thorough justice and the seriousness of sin.

questions.question: What was the punishment for the one found with the accursed thing, as stated in Joshua 7:15?
options: Burning with fire along with all that he had
A fine paid to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Burning with fire along with all that he had
questions.explanation: Verse 15 prescribes burning the guilty person and all possessions as punishment for transgressing God's covenant, showing the gravity of the offense.

questions.question: Which tribe was identified as having the guilty person when Joshua brought Israel by their tribes?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah
questions.explanation: According to Joshua 7:16, the tribe of Judah was taken first, indicating the beginning of the identification process pointing to the guilty party.

questions.question: Within the tribe of Judah, which family was specifically singled out during the search for the accursed?
questions.correctAnswer: The family of the Zarhites
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:17 states that the family of the Zarhites in Judah was taken, showing the narrowing down of the search from tribe to family.

questions.question: How did Joshua address Achan when he was identified and brought forward?
options: "My son, give glory to the LORD God of Israel and confess what you have done."
"You shall be punished immediately without trial."
"Tell us who else was involved in this sin."
questions.correctAnswer: "My son, give glory to the LORD God of Israel and confess what you have done."
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:19 shows Joshua's appeal to Achan to glorify God and confess, emphasizing repentance and truth before judgment.

questions.question: What did Achan admit to taking and hiding, according to Joshua 7:21?
options: A golden calf and silver coins
A Babylonish garment, silver, and a wedge of gold
A sacred scroll and precious stones
questions.correctAnswer: A Babylonish garment, silver, and a wedge of gold
questions.explanation: Verse 21 records Achan's confession that he coveted and took a Babylonish garment, 200 shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold weighing 50 shekels.

questions.question: What was the immediate action taken after Achan confessed and the stolen items were found?
options: The items were returned to Jericho
The items were laid out before the LORD and Achan was taken to judgment
The items were given to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: The items were laid out before the LORD and Achan was taken to judgment
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:23-24 describe how the stolen items were brought out before the LORD and Achan with all his possessions was taken to the valley for judgment.

questions.question: What was the outcome of Achan's sin for him and his household as recorded in Joshua 7:25?
options: They were stoned and burned with fire
questions.correctAnswer: They were stoned and burned with fire
questions.explanation: Verse 25 states that Achan, his family, and possessions were stoned and burned, showing the severe consequences of violating God's covenant.

questions.question: What was the significance of the place where Achan was judged, as explained in Joshua 7:26?
options: It became a city of refuge
It was named the valley of Achor to mark the event
It was dedicated to the LORD as a holy ground
It was where Joshua built an altar
questions.correctAnswer: It was named the valley of Achor to mark the event
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:26 tells that the place was called the valley of Achor to remember the incident, and the LORD turned from His fierce anger after judgment.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 7:10, God rebuked Joshua for lying on his face before the ark of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:10 records the LORD asking Joshua why he lies on his face, indicating a rebuke for his posture of despair without action.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 7:18 reveals that Achan was brought forward along with his entire household man by man.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 18 explicitly states that Joshua brought Achan and his household man by man, showing the thoroughness of the investigation.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 7:13, sanctifying the people was necessary because they could stand before their enemies even with the accursed thing among them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:13 clearly states that Israel cannot stand before their enemies until they remove the accursed thing, so sanctification is necessary to enable victory.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 7.

questions.question: What did Joshua ask Achan to do before confessing his sin?
options: Give glory to the LORD God of Israel
Offer a sacrifice to the LORD
Hide his sin to avoid shame
questions.correctAnswer: Give glory to the LORD God of Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua instructed Achan to give glory to the LORD God of Israel and confess his sin openly, as stated in Joshua 7:19.

questions.question: According to Achan's confession, which items did he take that were accursed?
options: A Babylonish garment, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold
A sword, a shield, and a helmet
An ephod, a golden calf, and silver coins
questions.correctAnswer: A Babylonish garment, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold
questions.explanation: Achan confessed taking a goodly Babylonish garment, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold as accursed spoils, according to Joshua 7:21.

questions.question: Where were the stolen items hidden according to Achan's confession?
options: In the earth in the midst of his tent
Under the altar of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: In the earth in the midst of his tent
questions.explanation: Achan admitted that the stolen items were hidden in the earth in the midst of his tent, as noted in Joshua 7:21.

questions.question: What method did Joshua use to identify the tribe, family, and individual who had taken the accursed thing?
options: He brought Israel by tribes, families, and households man by man
He used casting lots to identify the guilty party
He asked the priests to reveal the sinner by prophecy
He interrogated the elders of each tribe
questions.correctAnswer: He brought Israel by tribes, families, and households man by man
questions.explanation: Joshua sanctified the people and brought them forward by tribes, then families, and finally individuals to find the one who took the accursed thing, as explained in Joshua 7:14-18.

questions.question: Which tribe was identified as the one from which the accursed person came?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah
questions.explanation: The tribe of Judah was singled out during the identification process as the tribe containing the accursed person, as stated in Joshua 7:16.

questions.question: What was the name of the family within the tribe of Judah to which the accursed person belonged?
questions.correctAnswer: The Zarhites
questions.explanation: Joshua identified the family of the Zarhites within the tribe of Judah during the selection process, as seen in Joshua 7:17.

questions.question: Who was the individual identified as having taken the accursed thing?
questions.correctAnswer: Achan, the son of Carmi
questions.explanation: Achan, son of Carmi, was identified as the one who took the accursed thing, as stated in Joshua 7:1 and Joshua 7:18.

questions.question: What was the consequence prescribed for the person who took the accursed thing?
options: He shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath
He shall be exiled from Israel
He shall be imprisoned for life
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:15 declares that the one who takes the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire along with all his possessions because of his transgression of the covenant.

questions.question: What items and persons were taken with Achan to the valley of Achor for judgment?
options: His sons, daughters, oxen, asses, sheep, tent, and all that he had
His household servants and his possessions
questions.correctAnswer: His sons, daughters, oxen, asses, sheep, tent, and all that he had
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:24 records that Achan, his family, livestock, tent, and all he had were taken to the valley of Achor for judgment.

questions.question: How did the people of Israel execute the judgment on Achan?
options: They stoned him with stones and burned him with fire
They imprisoned him until his death
They banished him from the camp
They struck him with the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They stoned him with stones and burned him with fire
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:25 describes that all Israel stoned Achan with stones and then burned him with fire after stoning him.

questions.question: What was the significance of the name given to the place where Achan was executed?
options: It was called The valley of Achor, meaning 'trouble', reflecting the LORD's anger
It was named The valley of Blessing, symbolizing forgiveness
It was designated The valley of Victory, commemorating Israel's conquest
It was known as The valley of Silence, signifying mourning
questions.correctAnswer: It was called The valley of Achor, meaning 'trouble', reflecting the LORD's anger
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:26 explains the place was named The valley of Achor, meaning 'trouble', because the LORD turned from His anger there after judgment was executed.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD said He would no longer be with Israel unless the accursed was destroyed from among them.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:12 states that the LORD would not be with Israel anymore unless the accursed thing was destroyed from among them, confirming the answer as True.

questions.question: True or False: The accursed thing was taken by Achan from the city of Ai.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:1 specifies the accursed thing was taken from Jericho, not Ai, making the statement false.

questions.question: Which literary device is most evident in the method Joshua used to identify the sinner by descending from tribe to family to individual?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The process of sanctifying and bringing Israel forward by tribe, family, and individual forms an inclusio framing the discovery of the sinner, as shown in Joshua 7:13-18.

questions.question: Cross-reference: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of hidden sin causing communal consequences, as seen in Joshua 7?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Corinthians 5:6-7
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:6-7 discusses how a little leaven leavens the whole lump, echoing the communal impact of hidden sin as in Joshua 7:1-26.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What specific sin did Achan commit that caused Israel's defeat at Ai?
options: He took from the accursed thing
questions.correctAnswer: He took from the accursed thing
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:1 clearly states that Achan took of the accursed thing, which caused the LORD's anger against Israel leading to their defeat.

questions.question: What was the LORD's declared condition for His continued presence with Israel after their sin?
options: They must destroy the accursed from among them
questions.correctAnswer: They must destroy the accursed from among them
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:12 records God’s command that He will not be with Israel anymore unless they remove the accursed thing from among them.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed in His response to Israel’s sin in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and justice
questions.explanation: The LORD’s anger and refusal to remain with Israel until the sin was dealt with (Joshua 7:11-12) demonstrates His holiness and justice, intolerant of sin in His covenant people.

questions.question: How does Joshua 7:6 illustrate the proper human response to sin against God’s covenant?
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance and mourning before God
questions.explanation: Joshua rent his clothes and fell on his face before the ark, putting dust on his head (Joshua 7:6), showing deep repentance and humility before God.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of the command in Joshua 7:15 regarding the punishment for the accursed person?
options: It underscores the seriousness of covenant violation
It permits mercy and forgiveness without penalty
It encourages personal discretion in judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It underscores the seriousness of covenant violation
questions.explanation: Verse 15 commands that the person with the accursed thing be burnt with fire, emphasizing the grave consequences of breaching God’s covenant holiness.

questions.question: What does Joshua 7:10 reveal about God’s willingness to engage with human distress?
options: God calls Joshua to rise and confront the situation
God punishes Joshua for his grief
questions.correctAnswer: God calls Joshua to rise and confront the situation
questions.explanation: The LORD speaks to Joshua, urging him to get up and act instead of remaining prostrate, showing God’s readiness to guide and restore (Joshua 7:10).

questions.question: What does the selection process described in Joshua 7:14-18 teach about God's method of revealing sin in the community?
options: God reveals sin progressively from tribe to household to individual
God immediately reveals all sin publicly
God reveals sin only after a year
God reveals sin only through dreams
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals sin progressively from tribe to household to individual
questions.explanation: Verses 14-18 show God’s methodical process of identifying the guilty party by tribe, family, household, and then individual, illustrating divine order in judgment.

questions.question: How does the narrative in Joshua 7 connect to the broader redemptive story of Scripture?
options: It demonstrates the necessity of holiness and obedience in the covenant community
It teaches that sin has no consequences
It shows that God accepts all actions without judgment
It records the establishment of the monarchy
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates the necessity of holiness and obedience in the covenant community
questions.explanation: Joshua 7 highlights that God’s blessing depends on obedience and sanctification, a theme central to the entire biblical covenant relationship (Joshua 7:11-13).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is taught by the LORD’s anger being 'turned' after Achan’s punishment in Joshua 7:26?
options: God’s wrath is just but can be appeased through judgment
God’s anger is permanent and unyielding
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wrath is just but can be appeased through judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 26 shows that after dealing with sin through just punishment, God’s anger is removed, teaching the doctrine of righteous wrath balanced with mercy.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine commands for harsh punishment are evidence of an unjust God. What does Joshua 7:15-26 actually teach about God's justice and holiness?
options: God’s justice requires holiness and appropriate punishment for covenant breach
God arbitrarily punishes people without reason
God’s commands are based on human opinion
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice requires holiness and appropriate punishment for covenant breach
questions.explanation: The text (7:15-26) reveals that God's justice demands holiness and that sin within His covenant community must be judged to maintain His holy presence, demonstrating righteous judgment rather than arbitrary cruelty.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by Israel’s inability to stand before their enemies until sin was removed (Joshua 7:12-13)?
options: The doctrine of sanctification and corporate holiness
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of sanctification and corporate holiness
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 teach that Israel’s corporate sanctification was necessary to stand before enemies, emphasizing holiness as essential for God’s presence and blessing.

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from combining Joshua 7:1 and 7:21 concerning human temptation and sin?
options: Covetous desire can lead to direct covenant violation and communal judgment
Sin is insignificant and has no consequences
God condones secret sin when hidden
Human actions do not affect divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: Covetous desire can lead to direct covenant violation and communal judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 1 introduces the sin of taking the accursed thing, and verse 21 reveals Achan’s coveting of valuables, showing how personal greed causes covenant breach impacting the entire community.

questions.question: How does the narrative in Joshua 7 demonstrate God's attribute of omniscience?
options: God knew Achan’s sin even before it was discovered
God was unaware of the sin until told
questions.correctAnswer: God knew Achan’s sin even before it was discovered
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:11-12 shows God's precise knowledge of the sin and the sinner, revealing His omniscience in knowing hidden sins.

questions.question: What does Joshua’s question in 7:9 reveal about his concern for God’s reputation among the nations?
options: Joshua worries that Israel’s failure will cause God’s name to be dishonored
Joshua is unconcerned about God’s name
Joshua wants to hide the defeat
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua worries that Israel’s failure will cause God’s name to be dishonored
questions.explanation: In verse 9, Joshua expresses concern that surrounding nations will hear of Israel’s defeat and question God’s greatness, reflecting divine concern for His glory.

questions.question: What does Joshua 7:22-23 teach about the role of confession and public acknowledgment in dealing with sin?
options: Confession leads to exposure and communal judgment
Sin should be hidden to avoid shame
Confession results in immediate forgiveness without consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Confession leads to exposure and communal judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 22-23 show that after Achan’s confession, the stolen items were publicly brought out before the LORD and Israel, demonstrating confession’s role in confronting sin publicly.
